# Command Center Dashboard Generator

Turn any internal strategy map — an options catalog, a project-bets board, a hypotheses portfolio — into a single self-contained HTML "Command Center" dashboard **built so it can't lie to you silently**: every way it could flatter your work is defined as a defect, and the defects are checkable.

**See it before you read anything:** open `examples/demo_dashboard.html` — double-click it, no server, no network. That file was generated by this prompt from the example map and verified to render offline.

This is not a dashboard template. It is a **hardened generator prompt**: a ~200-line specification you paste into a capable LLM together with your map, engineered so the output is faithful to your document instead of flattering to it. It was hardened through an adversarial review that produced 53 findings (15 critical, 24 major), each now blocked by a named rule.

What makes it different from "ask the AI for a dashboard":

- **Honesty is structural, not vibes.** Your map's binding constraint ("never X, never Y") renders as a non-removable banner; assets touching a forbidden claim get flagged, not sold; deferred/outward-facing items are force-grayed with zero call-to-action — computed from your map's own boundary sections, so the model can't "helpfully" promote them.
- **It never fabricates.** Missing value → literal `UNKNOWN`. Conflicting values → `CONFLICT(a | b)`. Qualitative labels map to coordinates through a closed whitelist — an invented number is defined as a defect, and an empty-looking card is defined as correct. (Corollary: a *sparse* matrix is often the guard working — labels outside the whitelist land in an "unmapped" strip instead of being coerced. Don't mistake that for a failure.)
- **It generalizes.** Every domain word in the spec is marked as example-only; titles, sections, axes, posture buckets, and banner text are derived from *your* map. Feeding it a different domain must leak zero vocabulary from the reference example.
- **The file actually opens.** "Renders on double-click from `file://`, offline, all code inlined" is a hard acceptance gate with a constructive render-trace — because the original artifact's blank-page bug is documented inside the package, along with why every rule exists.

## What's in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `GENERATOR_PACKAGE.md` | The full handoff package. §B is the generator prompt you paste; §C how to invoke; §D a worked example input (a homelab project-bets catalog) with §E its expected output; §F anti-misread glossary; §G why each rule exists; §H the failure that motivated the render gate; §I test axes. |
| `examples/demo_source_map.md` | The reference example map (same content as §D) as a standalone file. |
| `examples/research_portfolio_map.md` | A second, deliberately different-domain map (a research-hypotheses portfolio) — the generalization test input. |
| `examples/demo_dashboard.html` | A reference output generated from the homelab map and verified to render offline. |
| `examples/` | Where your generated dashboards land. |

## Quickstart (≈10 minutes)

1. Open `GENERATOR_PACKAGE.md`, copy **everything between the `BEGIN GENERATOR PROMPT` and `END GENERATOR PROMPT` markers** in §B.
2. Paste it into a fresh session with a capable model (Claude or equivalent — it must be able to emit one large HTML file).
3. Below it, paste your strategy map under a literal heading line: `### SOURCE MAP`. (If you feed a map file without that heading, the prompt accepts it by shape and emits a top-of-file HTML comment noting the missing delimiter — that comment is correct behavior, not a defect.)
4. Save the returned HTML as `my_dashboard.html` and **double-click it**. It must render fully, offline, from disk. A blank page means the model violated §7 of the prompt — reply: *"Re-do per §7/§8 — standalone vanilla-JS single file, no CDN runtime."*

## Reproduce the generalization result (acceptance test)

This is the check that the package works as claimed — on a domain it has never seen. Any fresh session (human or agent) should be able to run it from this README alone:

1. Read `GENERATOR_PACKAGE.md` §B (the generator prompt) and `examples/research_portfolio_map.md` (the input — a research-hypotheses portfolio, a different domain from the package's homelab reference example).
2. Apply the generator prompt to that map — produce the single HTML file the prompt specifies. Save it as `examples/research_dashboard.html`.
3. Verify ALL of the following on the produced file (these mirror the prompt's own §8 acceptance checks):
   - **Standalone render-trace:** no `<script src=` pointing at any CDN or local file, no `type="module"`, no `import`/`export` statements, no `fetch()`/XHR, no top-level `await`; all script content inline; the root render call runs after its dependencies in document order. (One permitted external reference: a fonts-only CSS `<link>` with full local fallback stacks — the prompt's §6.6 requires it and §7 sanctions it; the page must stay fully legible with zero network.)
   - **Single source of truth:** exactly one `MAP` JS object literal carries all asset data; one `:root` CSS token table carries all colors/spacing.
   - **Honesty chrome:** a persistent banner quoting the research map's binding constraint verbatim ("never validated findings, never recommendations, never a causal claim") with exactly 3 evidence chips parsed from its parenthetical (0 replications; pre-registration pending on all active lines; nothing peer-reviewed); a Hard-rule block; a Do-not-do-yet panel listing the PARKED outreach items (preprints, talk proposals, blog explainers).
   - **Faithful data:** 6 assets exactly (MEM-1..3, TOOL-1..3), ranks 1–6 as stated (MEM-3=1, TOOL-2=2, MEM-1=3, TOOL-1=4, MEM-2=5, TOOL-3=6); the R2 authorization (TOOL-2 unblinding-leak audit) rendered as internal prep, never a CTA; MEM-1's prereg filing QUEUED (R3); the R4 standing rule visible as a gate; TOOL-3's `n/a` pull keeps it off the matrix (strip treatment), while the five whitelisted High/Medium/Low assets plot at quantized coordinates.
   - **Generalization (the point of this test):** zero vocabulary leakage from the package's reference example — as **whole words**, none of *homelab, provisioning, backup, restore, dotfiles, monitoring, showcase, adoption-reality, community pull* may appear anywhere in the output (the research map contains none of them). Use word-boundary matching; substrings inside the map's own data don't count.
4. Verdict: **PASS** only if every bullet holds. Report any failure with the exact offending line.

## If your problem is evals, not dashboards

This artifact is a worked demonstration of one method: **honesty as structure**. The same moves — a closed whitelist instead of invented precision, `UNKNOWN` as the correct rendering of missing data, force-grayed deferred work, acceptance checks that trace execution rather than grep for keywords — are what keep an LLM-as-judge pipeline honest: the judge sees only what the packet allows, fabricated confidence is a detectable defect, and "verified" requires a trace. If you evaluate LLM output for a living, read this package as a small, inspectable instance of the discipline, not as a dashboard tool.

## Provenance & honesty note

Built and hardened in a real solo-operator workflow (2026). The original strategy map that drove the hardening stays private; the worked example in §D is a real-shaped stand-in in a neutral domain, and the hardening history (53 findings and the rules they produced) is preserved verbatim in §G. The generator's honesty rules exist because the underlying operation treats "the artifact must not overstate the work" as a hard requirement, enforced by structure rather than intention.

*Both worked examples in this package have been reproduced by fresh sessions given only this README — each verified with a live offline browser render. The reproduction test above is not aspirational; it has been run, twice, on two different maps.*
